ADR-0055 §1 (as amended 2026-11-06, #30905, ruling record 6687830530) — `resolveCbpRelation` derives a `controlled_by_parent` object's master from exactly one `master_detail` field declared `required: true` that names a reference, or, with none, from the object's ONLY `master_detail`, declared `required: false` and naming a reference: an OPTIONAL master (`CbpRelation.optional`), picked by the spec's own `controlledByParentMasterOf` so the parse and this reader cannot name different fields. A detail row that names its master is read through it, and a required master's read leaf is byte-identical to before; a row whose master reference is empty is read through the null-master arm of `computeControlledByParentFilter` alone, by the row's owner (`owner_id`, only where the detail carries that column) and by View All on the detail; the write gate still refuses a write that leaves the reference empty. Anything else resolves `null`, which both halves treat as fail-closed (reads answer RLS_DENY_FILTER, writes throw MasterDetailRelationMissingError, 422 INVALID_METADATA), reported once per object per cache generation: no `master_detail`, two or more required ones, two or more with none required, and one whose `required` is not written at all (this reader tests `required === false`, never its absence, so an object that reached the registry without the parse resolves no master). Do NOT restore the retired fallback tiers (any `master_detail`, then a required `lookup`) or a first-by-field-order pick among two: they were never part of ADR-0055 §1, `ObjectSchema` refuses those shapes at parse, and a gate that derives access from a relation the parse refuses is the disagreement the step-18 semantic migration `cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired` closed. Do NOT widen the null-master arm past rows whose master reference is empty, or let View All on the detail open the master arm. The reference-SPELLING tolerance in the same reader is a different, deliberate decision and stays.

ADR-0106 D7 — getMetadataReadableFields differs from getReadableFields in exactly one place, and the asymmetry is the decision. On the DATA plane a caller resolving to zero permission sets falls OPEN, mirroring the engine middleware, because reporting a narrowing the data path would not enforce is its own drift. On the METADATA plane the same caller resolves the configured fallback permission set (the two-step /auth/me/permissions performs), so a guest-facing deployment's schema exposure is a deliberate permission-set decision rather than an accidental everything-default. Converging the two methods in either direction reverses this.

ADR-0123 D2 — an authenticated session with NO active organization is a legal state with fail-closed semantics, and the two sides are deliberately ASYMMETRIC: tenant-scoped reads resolve to nothing (Layer 0's deny sentinel, silent, HTTP 200) while tenant-scoped insert/update are REFUSED with a 403 whose message names the missing active organization. Step 3.7's no-active-organization refusal is that write half. Deleting it, or 'simplifying' it into the sibling forge guard, restores the state the ruling closed: the forge guard validates SUPPLIED organization_id values only, so a payload naming no tenant written by a caller having no tenant walks past it, lands with organization_id NULL, and is then hidden by the read wall from every reader including its own author. `delete` is absent on purpose (it places no row; the Layer 0 row wall already resolves its target to nothing), and the refusal must stay ordered AHEAD of the forge guard so a caller with no organization scope is told that, not that the value they supplied is foreign.

ADR-0138 D1 — for the guest envelope the owner stays unset, and only the scenario's own writers (a hook, a flow, an assignment rule) set it; so the seed-ownership claim this file runs on every `app:seeded` (`claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle`) and at the first promotion re-owns a NULL-owner row only when the seed reported landing on it (`readSeededRecordIds`, the `seed-settlement` contract's `seededRecordIds`), and widening that arm back to every unowned row hands guest-written and public-form rows to the platform admin on the next boot.
